ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a tangled fishing line, with a ring at the lower-left end and a section of free straight end on the right side. Multiple colored fish are distributed on the line, and the directions of the fishes' heads and tails differ; the line crosses in many places, but at a crossing one cannot switch to another line segment that appears to intersect. Reasoning: According to the method in the problem, start from the lower-left ring and trace along the same continuous line toward the free end on the right side. When encountering a fish, if in the tracing direction from the ring to the free end the fish head is met before the fish tail, then after being pulled straight this fish's head will face toward the ring. Tracing along the line can determine that: the right-middle green fish, the lower yellow fish, the central vertical blue fish, the upper yellow fish, the upper-left vertical green fish, and the far-right pink fish are all met head first; the remaining several are met tail first. Therefore there are 6 fish whose heads will face toward the ring.

raw_record.question_text: How many fish will have their heads pointing towards the ring when we straighten the line?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: there is one tangled fishing line/cord with a circular ring at the left end and a loose straight end at the far right, with multiple fish attached along the cord and their heads/tails visible. To solve, trace the single continuous cord starting at the ring and moving toward the loose right end, being careful at crossings to stay on the same strand rather than jumping to a crossing strand. For each fish encountered, decide whether its head is on the side closer to the ring: equivalently, while tracing from the ring to the loose end, count a fish if you meet its head before its tail. Straightening the line does not change this head-versus-tail order along the cord. Applying this trace to all fish in the picture gives 6 fish whose heads point toward the ring after the line is straightened.
